```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/planning.R")
power_res   <- readRDS("results/power.rds")
k_chosen    <- power_res$k[which(power_res$power >= pv$power)[1]]
power_at_k  <- power_res$power[power_res$k == k_chosen]
n_practices <- 2 * k_chosen
n_patients  <- round(n_practices * pv$m)
mcse_max    <- max(sqrt(power_res$power * (1 - power_res$power) / power_res$n_sim))

pct <- function(x, d = 0) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x)
```

*Demonstration document. The study, its sources and all numbers are invented.*

Version 1.0, 20 October 2026.

# Study design

DEMO-CRT is a planned cluster-randomised, controlled, parallel-group superiority trial in
general practices of a regional practice network. Practices are randomised 1:1, in
permuted blocks of four, to an electronic decision-support tool in the practice software
(intervention) or to usual care (control). When a consultation for an acute respiratory
tract infection is coded, the tool shows the current guideline recommendation on
antibiotic treatment. Each practice is observed for six months after randomisation.

# Primary endpoint and estimand

The primary endpoint is whether the prescribing decision at a patient's first
consultation for an acute respiratory tract infection in the observation period is
concordant with the national guideline. It is assessed from the practice records by
assessors blinded to the allocation.

The primary estimand is the effect of offering the decision-support tool to a practice,
compared with usual care, on guideline-concordant prescribing for adults with an acute
respiratory tract infection, expressed as an odds ratio for a practice with an average
practice effect. Practices that stop using the tool remain in the analysis as randomised
(treatment policy). Patients who consult more than once contribute their first
consultation only.

The decision support is expected to raise guideline-concordant prescribing from 45% to
60%.

# Planning values

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|:---------------------------------------------|:----------------|:---------------------------------------|
| Guideline-concordant prescribing, usual care | `r pct(pv$p0)` | Practice network audit 2024 (internal report) |
| Guideline-concordant prescribing, decision support | `r pct(pv$p1)` | Smallest increase of clinical interest, agreed with the investigators (steering committee, 18 June 2026) |
| Intracluster correlation (logit scale) | `r pv$icc` | Pilot study in 12 practices, 2025 (internal report) |
| Eligible patients per practice in six months, mean | `r pv$m` | Practice network audit 2024 (internal report) |
| Eligible patients per practice, coefficient of variation | `r pv$cv` | Practice network audit 2024 (internal report) |
| Significance level | `r pct(pv$alpha)`, two-sided | |
| Power | `r pct(pv$power)` | |

: Planning values. {#tbl-planning}

# Sample size

Because the primary analysis is a logistic mixed model and the practices differ in size,
we estimated power by simulation. For 6 to 16 practices per arm, we simulated
`r format(power_res$n_sim[1], big.mark = ",")` trials each under the planning values in
@tbl-planning: the number of eligible patients per practice from a gamma distribution
with the stated mean and coefficient of variation (at least 5), a normally distributed
practice effect on the logit scale with the variance that gives the stated intracluster
correlation, and one outcome per patient from the logistic model. Each simulated trial
was analysed with the primary analysis (Section 5); power is the share of trials with
p < 0.05 (@fig-power). The Monte Carlo standard error of each estimate is at most
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mcse_max)` percentage points.

```{r}
#| label: fig-power
#| fig-cap: "Estimated power by number of practices per arm. Dashed line: 80% power; dotted line: chosen number of practices."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.4
par(mar = c(4.2, 4.4, 0.8, 0.8))
plot(power_res$k, power_res$power, type = "b", pch = 19, ylim = c(0.4, 1), las = 1,
     xlab = "Practices per arm", ylab = "Estimated power")
abline(h = pv$power, lty = 2)
abline(v = k_chosen, lty = 3)
```

The smallest number of practices per arm with an estimated power of at least 80% is
`r k_chosen` (estimated power `r pct(power_at_k, 1)`). We will therefore randomise
`r n_practices` practices, which at a mean of `r pv$m` eligible patients per practice
gives about `r format(n_patients, big.mark = ",")` patients.

The simulation is in `R/simulate.R` and `sim/run_power.R`, with the planning values in
`R/planning.R`; the results are saved in `results/power.rds`, which this document reads.

# Analysis

The primary analysis is a logistic mixed model of guideline-concordant prescribing with
the intervention as fixed effect and a random intercept for practice, fitted by maximum
likelihood with the Laplace approximation. The intervention effect is tested with the
Wald test at the two-sided 5% level. The outcome is taken from the practice records, so
missing outcome data are not expected.

# Software

Simulations were run in `r R.version.string` with lme4 `r packageVersion("lme4")`. The
simulation code and the random seed are part of the source of this document.
